title: Lock a mailer's roll end: seat both tabs of the rolled inner panel in the base holes while one hand holds the wall up
instruction: Lock the near end of the mailer box, both tabs seated in the holes in the base and the wall's top flat: hold the end wall upright, roll its inner panel over the top and down inside until both tabs snap in, then move both hands clear.
context: Shipping, receiving, and inventory clerks (O*NET 43-5071.00; 816,870 US jobs, BLS OEWS May 2025) have the Core task 'Pack, seal, label, or affix postage to prepare materials for shipping, using hand tools, power tools, or postage meter.' Much of it goes in one-piece die-cut mailers that lock without tape or glue (FEFCO 0427). The lock is the roll end: Packlane's guide: 'snap each side panel into the holes in the bottom of the box, continuing the same motion.' This task is only that lock. The tuck flaps are already folded in behind the end wall, and they and the wall's crease spring it back open, so one hand must hold the wall upright while the other rolls the wall's inner panel over a double crease, two creases a wall's thickness apart, and pushes it down inside the box blind, so that its two tabs find their holes along the base crease. Rolled at one end only, the panel skews; pushed too hard, the board crushes. O*NET is a trademark of USDOL/ETA; task text used under CC BY 4.0.
setup: Station: two YAM arms with parallel grippers, bases 61 cm apart at the near edge of a 120 x 90 cm wood table, 75 cm high. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. Box: a FEFCO 0427 mailer (one piece, roll ends, tuck front, no glue) in B-flute corrugated board 3.2 mm thick (B flute's 1/8 in flute height), outside 13 3/8 x 12 3/8 x 6 1/4 in (34.0 x 31.4 x 15.9 cm), 0.45 kg: the outside size, board and mass of a 12 x 12 x 6 in tab-locking mailer (Uline S-16934). A rolled end is 17.5 mm thick, half of Uline's outside less inside length ((13 3/8 - 12) / 2 in): outer panel, the trapped tuck flaps and the inner panel. The die-line is a FEFCO 0427 template at that size: base; front and back walls, each with a 14 x 14 cm tuck flap at its near end; the near end's outer panel, 31.4 x 15.9 cm, joined over a double crease to its inner panel, 30.5 x 15.2 cm, with two 2.5 cm tabs on its free edge at y -8 and 8; two 6 x 30 mm holes for them in the base, 1.6 cm inside the near crease; the lid with its tuck. Start state, the same every trial: the base lies flat on the table, free (nothing holds it; board on the bench's laminate or wood, friction about 0.4: Park et al. 2019 give 0.38 static for board on board), its near crease along y at x 28 (y -15.7 to 15.7), the box running away from the robot to x 62. The far end is already locked. The front and back walls stand, their near tuck flaps folded in square across the end. The near end's outer panel leans back toward the robot at 75 +/- 5 degrees above the table, where its crease springs it, its inner panel unrolled beyond its top. The lid, hinged on the left wall's top, lies open to the robot's left, its front edge and tuck on the table. The box stays free: the hold on the end wall slides it under the hand, by about 3.5 cm in the demo, no hand or stop braces it, and the policy must finish the lock on a box that moves. Both grippers start at the arms' ready pose, 26 cm above the table at (32, 30.5) and (32, -30.5). In simulation (settings, not measurements: no published figure exists for B-flute creases): holding the end wall upright takes 3 N at its top edge; holding the inner panel rolled flat inside takes 0.2 N at its free edge (1.6 N 2 cm out from its crease), and unheld it springs back up; a tab pressed back 3 mm by the base bears on it with 0.45 N. Reset: unhook the tabs, roll the inner panel back out and let the wall spring back. Replace the box after 10 trials, or sooner once its end wall no longer rests at 75 +/- 5 degrees, as creases soften with use. A real trial uses S-16934 as bought; its own tabs and holes stand in for the modelled ones.
scoring: Measured at the end with photos from the front and from above, a ruler and a square; the tabs checked from underneath. Score 0, and it stays 0 for the rest of the trial, if the box is at any time pushed or lifted more than 5 cm (the demo's slide is at most 3.5 cm, so a slide that size is allowed), turned more than 10 degrees about the vertical or tipped more than 10 degrees, a tuck flap ends outside the end wall (swung out more than 30 degrees), or, in a real trial, the board is crushed: a dent or new fold deeper than 2 mm away from the die-cut creases. Otherwise the rungs are cumulative: 0.25 with the inner panel rolled over the top (folded past 100 degrees), its free edge inside the box and below the wall's top; 0.5 with the inner panel within 10 degrees of the outer panel and its free edge within 1 cm of the base; 0.75 with at least one tab in its hole; 1.0 with both tabs in their holes, the wall's top flat (both creases of the rolled top within 5 mm of the same height, by ruler: Packlane's check, 'the tops of the side walls are flat, not slanted or peaked'), the wall within 5 degrees of upright with both tuck flaps inside it (within 10 degrees of folded in), both grippers at least 3 cm from the box, and nothing moving more than 1 mm over 1 s. A tab is in its hole when its tip is at least 2 mm down into the base board, inside the hole's outline: in a real trial the box is tipped up after the photos and the seated tab's tip is seen in its hole from underneath.
fidelity: Board panels are rigid plates on sprung hinges; crease forces are simulation settings, not measurements. The double crease is one hinge, the rolled end 17.5 mm thick (Uline: outside less inside). A tab's give is a 5 mm sprung slide; pressed 2 mm into its hole it latches, and with both in the end is held locked, as seated tabs and trapped flaps hold a real one. The panel cannot twist. The box is free: 0.45 kg, friction 0.4 with the table (a setting, 0.38 static for board on board).
reset_notes: Nothing is random (object_jitter=0). Between real trials unhook the tabs, roll the inner panel back out and let the wall spring back; replace the box after 10 trials or once its end wall no longer rests at 75 +/- 5 degrees.
